solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Girl, pagan at heart, that's last to go

indicators.note: the heart of a word is everything inside its outer letters, so only the core of pagan is used
the final letter of that is dropped, as the clue says it must go

parts.note: the word that, with the 's read as 'is' joining it to what happens next

explanation.surface: A girl with a pagan streak is told she must be the last one out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' takes AGA from the middle of pagan; 'last to go' removes the final T of THAT to leave THA.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha is a female first name, and crossword 'girl' often stands for any woman's name.

clue.text: Find out glass at first not full

indicators.note: only the opening letter of glass is wanted here

parts.note: lean means thin or meagre, the opposite of full or plump

explanation.surface: Someone discovers that a glass of drink has not been filled to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: To glean is to gather information bit by bit, so it means to learn or discover.

clue.text: After mishap the limb provides protection for finger

indicators.note: a mishap leaves things in disarray, so the letters of the words that follow are jumbled

explanation.surface: After an accident to an arm, something is provided to guard a finger.
explanation.definitionFit: A thimble is the small metal cap a sewer wears to shield a fingertip from the needle.

clue.text: "Say when" used regularly brings wonderment!

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every second letter of the phrase is used

explanation.surface: Someone pouring a drink who is told to 'say when' keeps being amazed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say when' is what you say to someone pouring you a drink, inviting you to stop them.
explanation.definitionFit: Awe is a feeling of reverent amazement, the same emotion as wonderment.

clue.text: Office equipment shown by policeman? That is right

parts.note: cop is slang for a police officer
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Is the office machine being shown off by a police officer? Correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A copier, or photocopier, is a machine found in offices for duplicating documents.

clue.text: Case for explosive in vehicle on crest

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a cart is a simple wheeled vehicle
a crest is the top of a hill, a ridge

explanation.surface: Explosives are stashed in a car parked on the brow of a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartridge is the casing holding the powder charge, and often the bullet, for a gun.

clue.text: Play that amuses worker in Post Office?

indicators.note: the worker is placed inside the letters for the Post Office

parts.note: the worker ant is the crossword's favourite worker

explanation.surface: Is there a comic show that entertains a member of staff at the post office?
explanation.walkthrough: Panto, short for pantomime, is a British comic family stage show put on around Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantomime is a light comic theatre production meant purely to entertain an audience.

clue.text: Held up by the visa, very hard to pin down?

indicators.note: in a down entry, up says the hidden letters read from bottom to top
Held, completed by the later word by, says the letters are held inside the words that follow
by joins Held to say the answer is held by these words, hidden inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A traveller is delayed at a border because of a visa, and is very hard to track.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave the hiding no indicator: 'Held ... by' signals letters held inside the words, and 'up' says that in this down entry they read from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone evasive dodges questions or capture, so they are slippery and difficult to catch.

clue.text: Entered marina, rebuilt, much water there!

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boat came into a reconstructed marina, where there is plenty of sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean is a large sea between Europe and Africa, so a great deal of water is found there.

clue.text: Elitist initially seemed nervous over background

indicators.note: the opening letter of each of the next four words is taken

explanation.surface: A snooty person at first appeared anxious about where they came from.
explanation.definitionFit: A snob looks down on those of lower social standing, which is an elitist attitude.

clue.text: Mocking Caesar — not half! — backed by academic in charge

indicators.note: the first piece has the next pieces placed behind it
losing half of Caesar leaves only its back half of letters

parts.note: a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A Roman emperor, cut down to size, is supported by a scholar in command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' drops CAE from Caesar to leave SAR. 'Not half!' is also British slang for 'very much so'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardonic describes grimly scornful humour, a scoffing and derisive manner.

clue.text: Some present I mentioned giving opinion

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A speaker refers to a gift they have talked about while offering a view.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentiment is a view or attitude held about something, as when one voices a feeling.

clue.text: Raver loses head in Tennessee pub

indicators.note: the shortened raver goes inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: TN is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Tennessee

indicators.note: the first letter of raver is cut off

explanation.surface: A partygoer gets knocked out cold in a Tennessee bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A tavern is an inn or public house where drinks are served.

clue.text: Like graduate mother in US State

parts.note: à la is French for in the style of, meaning like
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Following in a graduate mother's footsteps, someone settles in an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabama is one of the fifty states of America, in the Deep South.

clue.text: Barriers met by the Spanish girl, old-fashioned

parts.note: dams are barriers that hold back water
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: An old-world Spanish girl encounters obstacles in her path.
explanation.definitionFit: Damsel is an archaic word for a young unmarried woman, as in a damsel in distress.

clue.text: Unusually unnamed, unexciting

indicators.note: letters arranged in an unusual way are put into a different order

explanation.surface: Something without a name is, oddly enough, dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Mundane means ordinary and humdrum, lacking any interest or thrill.

clue.text: March round island — a perfect location

indicators.note: the march goes round the island, enclosing its letters

parts.note: a parade is a ceremonial march

explanation.surface: Marchers circle an island, which turns out to be an ideal spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is a heavenly or idyllic place, the ideal setting.

clue.text: A soldier on lake with energy, nimble

indicators.note: in a down clue the soldier sits on top of what follows

parts.note: GI is a US army private
L is the map abbreviation for lake
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A soldier out on the lake is full of beans and quick on his feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Agile and nimble both describe someone quick and light in movement.

clue.text: In New York on return so inquisitive

indicators.note: the turned-round word sits inside the city abbreviation
returning means the word so is read backwards

explanation.surface: Back in New York, someone is consequently very curious.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosy describes someone prying into others' affairs, overly curious.

clue.text: Exhausted writer in street

indicators.note: the writer is placed inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: An author living on a particular road is worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent means used up or tired out, the same as worn out.

clue.text: A private's keen to reform one who's not had to learn the language

definitions.text: one who's not had to learn the language

indicators.note: to reform something is to shape it anew, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An army private is eager to mend his ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A native speaker grew up using a language from birth, so never had to study it as a foreign tongue.

clue.text: Liveliness the same after upset

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, and this word reads identically from bottom to top

parts.note: energy or liveliness

explanation.surface: Someone's high spirits are unchanged despite a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is the whole answer: turned over, it reads just as before.
explanation.definitionFit: Pep is energy and vigour, a synonym for liveliness.

clue.text: Extremely alert after grotto warning

indicators.note: the alert letters come after the grotto word

parts.note: a grotto is a small cave

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, so only those of alert are used

explanation.surface: A cave explorer is told to stay very watchful.
explanation.definitionFit: A caveat is a caution or proviso, Latin for 'let him beware'.

clue.text: Very many made advances in wings of party

indicators.note: the loan word sits inside the outer letters of party
the wings of something are its two sides, so the first and last letters of party

parts.note: lent means advanced money as a loan

explanation.surface: At the party, people made many passes at one another.
explanation.definitionFit: Plenty means a large quantity, more than enough, as in plenty of people.
